whenToUse: Forms with many fields, such as orders, sign-up, or applications.
The next step depends on earlier answers.
People must review everything once before submitting.
whenNotToUse: Forms with only a few fields (one screen is faster).
Settings screens edited in any order (use tabs or sections).
People often need to skip steps.

alternatives.name: Tabs
alternatives.reason: Settings people move between in any order.

alternatives.name: Error Summary
alternatives.reason: Gathering errors on a one-screen form.

accessibility: The progress list marks the current step with aria-current="step" and also shows "Step 2 of 3" in words.
When the step changes, move focus to the new step's heading so people hear where they are.
Going back keeps the values people entered.
The next button submits a form, so Enter also advances, and only after the step passes validation.
